title_en: China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., Jinan Branch v. Linqing Xin Yinhe Industrial Co., Ltd. and Zhongye Paper Yinhe Co., Ltd. — dispute over a financial loan contract
ruling_gist_en: The minutes of the meeting of the creditors' committee are the embodiment of the collective will of the creditors' committee and represent the true intent of each member unit of the creditors' committee. They do not violate the provisions of laws and regulations, and each member unit shall comply with them. If a member of the creditors' committee has promised to act in concert with other members and shall not, except with the consent of the creditors' committee, dispose of creditor's rights individually or jointly with other parties (including but not limited to filing lawsuits, seizure, sale, auction, garnishment, etc.), and if, before the expiration of the performance period stipulated in the debt restructuring agreement, such member files a separate lawsuit to claim realization of its creditor's rights without the consent of the creditors' committee, the people's court shall render a judgment to dismiss its claims.

full_text_en:
China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., Jinan Branch v. Linqing XinYinhe Industrial Co., Ltd. and MCC Paper Yinhe Co., Ltd. — dispute over financial loan contract

Ruling Summary

The minutes of a meeting of the creditors' committee embody the collective will of the committee and represent the true intentions of each member unit. They do not violate laws or administrative regulations, and each member unit shall comply with and implement them. Where a member of the creditors' committee commits to act in concert with other members and agrees not to dispose of creditor's rights (including but not limited to filing lawsuits, attaching property, selling, auctioning, or deducting funds) individually or jointly with others without the consent of the committee, if such member files a separate lawsuit to claim its creditor's rights before the expiration of the performance period stipulated in the debt restructuring agreement, without the consent of the committee, the people's court shall render a judgment dismissing its claims.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Ruling
(2021) Supreme People's Court Civil Application No. 2707

Reapplying Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., Jinan Branch, domiciled at Building 1, Zone 4, Hanyu Financial Business Center, No. 7000 Jingshi Road, High-Tech Zone, Jinan City, Shandong Province.

Responsible Person: Xin Liang, President of the Branch.

Agent Ad Litem: Liu Yang, In-House Counsel of the Branch.

Agent Ad Litem: Ma Wen, In-House Counsel of the Branch.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Linqing XinYinhe Industrial Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 297 Ximenli Street, Linqing City, Liaocheng City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Li Yi, General Manager of the Company.

Agent Ad Litem: Liu Jinhai, Lawyer at Beijing Weiheng (Jinan) Law Firm.

Agent Ad Litem: Liu Jiheng, Lawyer at Beijing Weiheng (Jinan) Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): MCC Paper Yinhe Co., Ltd., domiciled at Ximenli Street, Linqing City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Li Yi, General Manager of the Company.

Agent Ad Litem: Zhao Hongwen, Employee of the Company.

Agent Ad Litem: Liu Jinhai, Lawyer at Beijing Weiheng (Jinan) Law Firm.

The reapplying appellant, China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., Jinan Branch (hereinafter referred to as Jinan CMB), filed an application with this Court for retrial of the case concerning a dispute over a financial loan contract with the respondents, Linqing XinYinhe Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as XinYinhe Company) and MCC Paper Yinhe Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as MCC Yinhe Company), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2020) Lu Min Zhong No. 450 rendered by the Shandong High People's Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to review the case. On June 24, 2021, this Court conducted an inquiry. The agents ad litem of Jinan CMB, Liu Yang and Ma Wen, the agents ad litem of XinYinhe Company, Liu Jinhai and Liu Jiheng, and the agents ad litem of MCC Yinhe Company, Zhao Hongwen and Liu Jinhai, appeared before the court to participate in the proceedings. The review of this case has now been concluded.

Jinan CMB filed its application for retrial, alleging: First, Jinan CMB sent representatives to attend the creditors' meeting on May 22, 2019, and clearly stated to other members of the creditors' committee, XinYinhe Company, and MCC Yinhe Company that if XinYinhe Company and MCC Yinhe Company did not rectify their breach of contract, it would downgrade the management of the non-performing loan and seek legal remedies in accordance with the law. The minutes of the meeting did not undergo a voting procedure, and the matters recorded were not voted upon. Furthermore, the minutes of the meeting expressly stipulate that the handling of loan renewals and rollovers by creditor banks is subject to the precondition that XinYinhe Company and its affiliates do not breach the contract. Given that XinYinhe Company and MCC Yinhe Company still failed to perform their obligations under the debt restructuring agreement and the loans in question became overdue, Jinan CMB was lawfully entitled to file a lawsuit. After Jinan CMB filed the lawsuit, no creditor bank in the committee raised any objection. During the second instance, only one of the 14 creditor banks, the Liaocheng Branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, opposed Jinan CMB's lawsuit. The creditor banks had reached a consensus on the breach of contract by XinYinhe Company and MCC Yinhe Company and tacitly approved or supported Jinan CMB's approach of "using litigation to promote performance." The second instance ruling that the minutes of the meeting established that Jinan CMB and other creditor banks had granted a certain grace period for the breach of contract by XinYinhe Company and MCC Yinhe Company lacked evidence. Second, whether XinYinhe Company and MCC Yinhe Company continued to breach the contract after the creditors' meeting on May 22, 2019, is a key fact in this case. The second instance found that XinYinhe Company and MCC Yinhe Company failed to repay a loan principal amount of one-thousandth of their loan balance due to reasons attributable to Jinan CMB and the Liaocheng Branch of China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd. The evidence supporting this finding was not subjected to cross-examination by Jinan CMB, and the finding of fact was erroneous. Third, this case concerns a dispute over a financial loan contract. The Framework Agreement, Implementation Plan, and Supplementary Plan involved in this case stipulate that XinYinhe Company and MCC Yinhe Company must first perform three contractual obligations: asset transfer, capital increase, and repayment of the outstanding loan principal. However, as of the date Jinan CMB filed the lawsuit, they had not performed any of these obligations. As the party required to perform first, XinYinhe Company and MCC Yinhe Company, having failed to perform, are not entitled to demand performance from the party required to perform later. The second instance failed to apply the provision of Article 67 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law), which entitles the party required to perform later to refuse performance, and thus incorrectly applied the law. Fourth, the loan contract of 2018 was signed after the Framework Agreement, Implementation Plan, and Supplementary Plan, and served as the direct basis for the disbursement of the loans in this case. This contract stipulated that the loan would mature on June 18, 2019. The earlier Framework Agreement, Implementation Plan, and Supplementary Plan contained unclear provisions regarding the loan term. Jinan CMB was entitled to demand loan repayment from XinYinhe Company in accordance with the 2018 loan contract and Article 206 of the Contract Law, which provides for repayment when the loan term is unclear. Furthermore, the Linqing City People's Government did not affix its seal to the Supplementary Plan, rendering it ineffective. The second instance's confirmation of the validity of the Supplementary Plan lacked factual and legal basis. Fifth, according to the Notice of the General Office of the China Banking Regulatory Commission on Improving the Work of Creditors' Committees of Banking Financial Institutions (Yin Jian Ban Bian Han [2016] No. 1196), the creditors' committee is by nature a consultative, self-regulatory, and temporary organization, and its function is to lawfully protect the legitimate rights and interests of banking financial institutions. The various "creditor agreements" formed by the creditors' committee are arrangements of rights and obligations among the creditor banks, and do not constitute "commitments to roll over loans" to the debtor enterprises. Whether Jinan CMB's filing of the lawsuit constituted a breach of contract towards other creditor banks and the extent of such breach exceeded the scope of the plaintiff's claims and is not within the scope of trial for a dispute over a financial loan contract. Jinan CMB filed the lawsuit because XinYinhe Company and MCC Yinhe Company fundamentally breached the agreement, frustrating the purpose of the debt restructuring contract. This does not constitute a so-called "arbitrary" withdrawal of loans or cessation of lending. Jinan CMB filed the lawsuit in accordance with the law and the agreement. The second instance's finding that Jinan CMB violated the principle of good faith was erroneous. Sixth, even if the second instance court believed that Jinan CMB filed the lawsuit without prior authorization from the creditors' committee and unilaterally, and should have found that Jinan CMB lacked standing as a plaintiff, and applied Article 119, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China to dismiss the lawsuit by ruling, the second instance's judgment dismissing Jinan CMB's claims was an incorrect application of the law. In summary, Jinan CMB applied for retrial based on Items 2, 4, and 6 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, requesting a retrial of this case.

XinYinhe Company and MCC Yinhe Company submitted their opinions, contending that Jinan CMB, as a beneficiary of the debt restructuring agreement, filed a separate lawsuit while the loans had not yet matured, thereby harming the legitimate rights and interests of XinYinhe Company, MCC Yinhe Company, other creditor banks, and the general public. Even if XinYinhe Company and MCC Yinhe Company had breached the contract, the parties to the debt restructuring agreement were the creditors' committee and all creditor banks. Jinan CMB, as a single member of the creditors' committee, was not entitled to file a separate lawsuit. The debt restructuring agreement expressly stipulated that the minimum loan term was eight years. The loan contracts were executed in performance of the debt restructuring agreement. In 2016, Jinan CMB issued a written certificate promising to renew the loans upon maturity until the principal and interest of the restructured loans were fully repaid, which constituted a clear acknowledgment of the minimum eight-year loan term. In summary, the second instance's findings of fact were clear, the application of law was correct, and the procedural law was complied with. They requested the dismissal of Jinan CMB's application for retrial.

This Court is of the opinion that the focus of this review is on the following four issues: the validity of the series of restructuring agreements, including the Framework Agreement, Implementation Plan, and Supplementary Plan; the relationship between the 2018 loan contract and the series of restructuring agreements; the validity of the minutes of the meeting dated May 22, 2019; and the specific method of adjudication in this case.

I. Regarding the validity of the series of restructuring agreements, including the Framework Agreement, Implementation Plan, and Supplementary Plan. In this case, the series of debt restructuring agreements, including the Framework Agreement, Implementation Plan, and Supplementary Plan, were signed under the impetus of the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council, the Linqing City People's Government, and the Liaocheng Banking Association, for the purpose of handling the debts of MCC Yinhe Company, ensuring that the loan principals of the creditor banks would not be lost, and maintaining the normal operation of the high-quality assets of MCC Yinhe Company. These agreements do not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations and are all valid. The Linqing City People's Government acted as a supervisor in the Supplementary Plan, supervising and assisting in the implementation and fulfillment of the agreed terms. The failure of the Linqing City People's Government to affix its seal does not affect the validity of the Supplementary Plan. During the retrial review, the Linqing City People's Government also issued a certificate stating that the government played a supervisory role and, although it did not affix its seal to the Supplementary Plan, it has recognized the validity of the Supplementary Plan from the outset.

II. Regarding the relationship between the 2018 loan contract involved in this case and the series of restructuring agreements. The debt restructuring agreements involved in this case expressly stipulate that the loans assumed by XinYinhe Company shall be renewed upon maturity until the restructured loans are fully repaid. After the loans assumed by XinYinhe Company mature, and before the principal and interest of the restructured loans are fully settled, each creditor bank shall take measures such as "repaying the old with the new" to ensure that the loans are renewed upon maturity. The 2015 loan contract signed between the Liaocheng Branch of China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd. and XinYinhe Company, as well as the 2018 loan contract signed between Jinan CMB and XinYinhe Company, were both performances of the obligations under the debt restructuring agreement. Moreover, the 2018 loan contract expressly stipulates that the loan purpose is to repay the old with the new. The second instance's finding that the 2018 loan contract was a loan for repaying the old with the new disbursed based on the series of restructuring agreements, and not a new agreement between the parties regarding the loan matters, is correct. Jinan CMB, as a signatory to the series of restructuring agreements, is bound by them. According to the series of restructuring agreements, the term for the loans assumed by XinYinhe Company is eight years. Each creditor bank shall ensure the renewal of the loans upon maturity through methods such as repaying the old with the new. By the time Jinan CMB filed this lawsuit, the agreed term had not yet expired.

III. Regarding the validity of the minutes of the meeting dated May 22, 2019. The creditors' committee operated within the framework of the series of restructuring agreements. The parties, including Jinan CMB, signed multiple agreements. Among them, the Supplementary Plan expressly stipulates that no party shall unilaterally or jointly with others reach any agreement with the debtor concerning its creditor's rights other than the Supplementary Plan, and shall not individually or jointly with others dispose of the debtor's assets (including but not limited to filing lawsuits, attaching property, selling, auctioning, or deducting funds) without the consent of the creditors' committee. Article 3, Paragraph 4 further stipulates that if any member of the creditors' committee fails to perform the Implementation Plan and the Supplementary Plan, withdraws funds, or unilaterally takes preservation actions in breach of the agreement, it shall correct such actions within a date specified by the creditors' committee. If a creditor fails to timely correct its breach, it shall compensate other creditors for their losses. On May 22, 2019, MCC Yinhe Company and the creditor banks held a creditors' meeting and produced the minutes of the meeting. In the minutes, the creditor banks agreed to grant a grace period for the breach of contract by XinYinhe Company and MCC Yinhe Company, given that XinYinhe Company had failed to increase capital as stipulated in the series of restructuring agreements and MCC Yinhe Company had failed to incorporate its high-quality assets into XinYinhe Company as required by the debt restructuring agreement. Jinan CMB also sent representatives to attend this meeting. This Court is of the opinion that the creditors' committee is a consultative, self-regulatory, and temporary organization established by creditor banking financial institutions. It must both support the development of the real economy and lawfully protect the legitimate rights and interests of financial institutions. When a debtor fails to perform an agreement, the creditors' committee may, in conjunction with financial institutions, issue warnings to the relevant enterprise, require it to rectify within a specified period, promptly report relevant information to member units, and share information with relevant national credit information platforms through appropriate means, imposing sanctions for dishonesty on enterprises that evade financial debts in accordance with laws and regulations. For enterprises that evade financial debts and refuse to take corrective measures, the creditors' committee may organize financial institutions to impose sanctions, such as refraining from granting new financing or, depending on the circumstances, reducing existing financing. Members of the creditors' committee shall act in concert. Jinan CMB, as a signatory to the series of restructuring agreements, committed to acting in concert with other creditor banks and shall implement the decisions of the creditors' committee. The minutes of the meeting dated May 22, 2019, are a continuation of the series of restructuring agreements and represent the common will reached after joint consultation by the creditors' committee. Furthermore, the minutes of the meeting comply with the conditions stipulated in the Notice of the General Office of the China Banking Regulatory Commission on Improving the Work of Creditors' Committees of Banking Financial Institutions (Yin Jian Ban Bian Han [2016] No. 1196), which require that major matters of the creditors' committee must, in principle, simultaneously meet two conditions: approval by members representing more than two-thirds of the total amount of financial creditor's rights and approval by more than half of all members of the creditors' committee. Therefore, the minutes of the meeting dated May 22, 2019, are valid. Where no other creditor bank raised any objection, Jinan CMB unilaterally failed to implement the minutes of the meeting and filed a separate lawsuit, which lacks factual and legal basis.

IV. Regarding the specific method of handling this case, whether to dismiss the claims or dismiss the lawsuit. Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A lawsuit must meet the following conditions: (1) the plaintiff is a citizen, legal person, or other organization that has a direct interest in the case; (2) there is a definite defendant; (3) there are specific claims, facts, and reasons; and (4) the case falls within the scope of civil litigation accepted by the people's court and is within the jurisdiction of the court where the lawsuit is filed." Dismissal of a lawsuit addresses procedural issues, while a judgment dismissing the claims addresses substantive rights and obligations. Jinan CMB's filing of the lawsuit complied with the legal requirements; it had standing as a plaintiff. The people's court lawfully accepted the case and did not dismiss the lawsuit by ruling, which is not improper. In this case, the members of the creditors' committee agreed that, without the consent of the committee, no member may individually or jointly with others dispose of the debtor's assets by means including filing lawsuits, attaching property, selling, auctioning, or deducting funds. This agreement embodies the collective will of the creditors' committee and represents the true intentions of each member unit, and does not violate laws or administrative regulations. Jinan CMB, as a member of the creditors' committee, committed to acting in concert with other creditor banks. Having failed to obtain the consent of the creditors' committee and before the performance period stipulated in the debt restructuring agreement had arrived, the creditor's rights it claimed in this case did not yet meet the conditions for realization. The second instance's judgment dismissing its claims is not improper.

In summary, Jinan CMB's application for retrial does not meet the circumstances provided for in Items 2, 4, and 6 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 204, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 395, Paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled as follows:

The application for retrial by China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., Jinan Branch is dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Lin Wenxue
Judge: Liu Chongli
Judge: Ge Hongtao

September 27, 2021

Judge Assistant: Yang Ting
Clerk: Song Yadong
